justification: Inspected `byte-buddy-dep/src/main/java/net/bytebuddy/implementation/bytecode/TypeCreation.java` and `byte-buddy-dep/src/test/java/net/bytebuddy/implementation/bytecode/TypeCreationTest.java`. The class is only 37 lines long, has one field, one protected constructor, one static factory (`of`) that only validates instantiability, and one `apply` method that emits `NEW` via ASM; it implements a single cohesive responsibility rather than multiple separable concerns. The test file exercises exactly those two behaviors (valid creation and rejection of array/primitive/abstract types), which supports low complexity and no evidence of insufficient modularization.
